synopsis: YVO Monthly Update: background seismicity and deformation, small hydrothermal explosion at Biscuit Basin
sections: Yellowstone Caldera activity remains at background levels, with 77 located earthquakes in September (largest = M3.4). Deformation measurements indicate no significant uplift or subsidence of the caldera or north caldera rim for the past several months. A small hydrothermal explosion occurred at Biscuit Basin on September 27.

During September 2026, the University of Utah Seismograph Stations, responsible for the operation and analysis of the Yellowstone Seismic Network, located 77 earthquakes in the Yellowstone National Park region. The largest event of the month was a minor earthquake of magnitude 3.4 located about 20 miles northeast of Moran, WY, on September 6 at 10:25 p.m. MDT. September seismicity in Yellowstone was marked by a small swarm of 24 earthquakes located about 7 miles north-northwest of West Yellowstone, MT, on September 8. The magnitudes ranged from -0.1 to 2.8. Earthquake activity in Yellowstone is at background levels.

Data from continuous GPS stations indicate little net deformation of the caldera or north caldera regions over the past several months. Subtle variations in ground motion are probably caused by seasonal variations associated with groundwater conditions as summer transitions to fall.

Black Diamond Pool in Biscuit Basin, the site of a hydrothermal explosion on July 23, 2024, had several eruptions during the latter half of the month, including one large event that sent water and mud tens of feet into the air on the night of September 23. Just after 8:12 PM MDT on September 27, the small pool that formed after the June 13, 2026, hydrothermal explosion was the source of a hydrothermal explosion that threw boiling water, steam, mud, and rocks at least 100 feet (30 meters) into the air. Giant Geyser erupted on September 10 and 22, its fourth and fifth eruptions of the year. Steamboat Geyser had only sporadic minor eruptions during the month.
